From 35eaa6d8d6c2ee65e96f507add856e0eacf24591 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Nikola Z. Ivanov" <zlatistiv@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 23:14:34 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] netdevsim: zero initialize struct iphdr in dummy sk_buff

Syzbot reports a KMSAN uninit-value originating from
nsim_dev_trap_skb_build, with the allocation also
being performed in the same function.

Fix this by calling skb_put_zero instead of skb_put to
guarantee zero initialization of the whole IP header.

Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=23d7fcd204e3837866ff
Fixes: da58f90f11f5 ("netdevsim: Add devlink-trap support")
Signed-off-by: Nikola Z. Ivanov <zlatistiv@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260426201434.742030-1-zlatistiv@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/netdevsim/dev.c b/drivers/net/netdevsim/dev.c
index 1e06e781c835..f00fc2f9ebde 100644
--- a/drivers/net/netdevsim/dev.c
+++ b/drivers/net/netdevsim/dev.c
@@ -829,7 +829,7 @@ static struct sk_buff *nsim_dev_trap_skb_build(void)
 	skb->protocol = htons(ETH_P_IP);
 
 	skb_set_network_header(skb, skb->len);
-	iph = skb_put(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr));
+	iph = skb_put_zero(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr));
 	iph->protocol = IPPROTO_UDP;
 	iph->saddr = in_aton("192.0.2.1");
 	iph->daddr = in_aton("198.51.100.1");
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a KMSAN uninitialized value bug in the `netdevsim` driver reported by Syzbot. The issue occurred in the `nsim_dev_trap_skb_build` function when constructing a dummy `sk_buff` for devlink-trap testing.

### Modifications per file

**File: `drivers/net/netdevsim/dev.c`**
- In the function `nsim_dev_trap_skb_build`, the call to `skb_put(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr))` is replaced with `skb_put_zero(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr))`.

### Relationships between modifications

- The change is **minimal and targeted**: only a single line in one file is altered.
- The relationship is that the fix ensures the entire IP header struct (`struct iphdr`) is zero-initialized before manually setting specific fields (`protocol`, `saddr`, `daddr`). Previously, only these three fields were assigned, leaving the rest of the header uninitialized, which triggered the KMSAN warning. By using `skb_put_zero`, all header bytes are set to zero, eliminating the uninitialized value issue.
- The modification is directly related to the bug report and the `Fixes` commit `da58f90f11f5` which introduced the original trap building code.
